newsitem.title: USA: SEC, U.S. attorney subpoena bond records.
newsitem.headline: SEC, U.S. attorney subpoena bond records.

text.p: A Dade County Commissioner linked in press reports to an alleged bond kickback scheme said Friday that federal investigators have subpoenaed county bond-dealing records.

The commissioner, James Burke, said, "They've subpoenaed documents from the finance department and I've encouraged them (department staff) to send more than they subpoenaed because I want to get the full story of what happened."
Both the U.S. Attorney's Office and the Securities and Exchange Commission subpoenaed the records, Burke told Reuters.
Neither the U.S. Attorney's office nor the SEC would comment on the probe.
Burke, who was chairman of the finance committee that oversees county bond issues, described the subpoenae as "further fishing."

Burke, who is black, said he believes investigators were probing "primarily the minority transactions and black firms" because he has been an advocate for including minority-owned firms in bond deals.
"I've said from the rostrum that things are not going to be fair until you have inclusion of black firms, particularly at the senior level," Burke said.

The Miami Herald has reported that FBI videotapes show Calvin Grigsby, the former president of the California firm Grigsby Brandford & Co., allegedly offering Burke a $300,000 kickback in exchange for steering bond business to the firm.
The conversation allegedly took place last month in a San Francisco hotel where Burke, Grigsby and Miami municipal bond firm owner Howard Gary discussed the kickbacks, the newspaper said.
Burke denied wrongdoing.

"There has been no bribery," Burke said. "One of the things that will become clear is that under our rules and procedures we have in place, the kind of one-person manipulation that has been alleged cannot happen."
Burke said he has seen the videotape and that it depicts a conversation manipulated by a government informant.

Burke did not identify the informant but the Miami Herald has reported that Gary was cooperating with investigators and secretly recorded conversations implicating Grigsby and Burke in bribery and kickback schemes.
"They made it sound like a locked case. If it was a locked case, they would have gone out and indicted," Burke said.
He said neither he nor his lawyer had been advised of any time frame for possible arrests.

"The government has an informant ... that they sent fishing and most of the tapes and videos they have are going to show the informant doing pretty much most of the talking and orchestrating, and will not show any activity by other people, particularly by me, other than talking and responding to them more as a friend," Burke said.
An official at Howard Gary & Co. said Gary had no comment, and the FBI also declined to comment.
No charges have been filed in connection with the Dade County bond allegations.

Regarding allegations in press reports that he steered to Grigsby Brandford a $183 million revenue bond refunding for a recyling plant, he said the firm was selected as senior manager by the plant owner in response to an unsolicited proposal from Grigsby Brandford.
Other Dade County finance officials have said the underwriter was selected by recycling plant officials, and not by the county.

The other deal linked to the allegations, a tentative $165 million revenue bond issue for a new basketball arena, was awarded to Grigsby Brandford because they were next in line among the county's standing pool of bond underwriters, Burke said.
"It was part of our regular rotation," he said.
